title: RAG Pipeline Overview
description: Trace how a question can move through documents, chunks, embeddings, retrieval, context assembly, and a grounded LLM response.

starter_files.content:
# RAG Pipeline Overview

This planning lesson uses static metadata only. It does not call embedding models, query a vector database, or generate an LLM response.

learning_objectives: Identify the major stages in a RAG pipeline.
Explain why documents are chunked before retrieval.
Describe how citations connect an answer back to source material.
Recognize hallucination risk points in retrieval and response generation.

pipeline_nodes.label: Document
pipeline_nodes.description: A trusted source document is available for retrieval.

pipeline_nodes.label: Chunker
pipeline_nodes.description: The document is split into a retrievable chunk.

pipeline_nodes.label: Embedding Model
pipeline_nodes.description: Mock embedding metadata represents text for similarity search.

pipeline_nodes.label: Vector Store
pipeline_nodes.description: The mock vector store indexes chunk metadata for retrieval.

pipeline_nodes.label: Retriever
pipeline_nodes.description: Retrieval selects the most relevant chunk for the query.

pipeline_nodes.label: Context Builder
pipeline_nodes.description: The query and retrieved source are assembled for the LLM.

pipeline_nodes.label: LLM
pipeline_nodes.description: A future model would generate a response from the assembled context.

pipeline_nodes.label: Response
pipeline_nodes.description: The planned response should stay grounded in the retrieved source.

pipeline_nodes.label: Citation
pipeline_nodes.description: The citation links the response claim to the retrieved chunk.

pipeline_nodes.label: Risk
pipeline_nodes.description: Unsupported claims are a hallucination risk point.

hints: Follow the pipeline from the user query to the cited response.
Chunks are the pieces the retriever can search over.
A response is stronger when each important claim points back to a source.
